r: This retry loop hammers the payment gateway the way a toddler hammers an elevator button. Five attempts at a fixed 200 ms interval mean a 2-second outage burns the whole budget before the upstream recovers. Every client, synchronized by the same deploy, stampedes back in lockstep, a thundering herd on a timer. Switch to exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance) and wrap the call in a circuit breaker. The catch block swallows every exception, including 400-series validation errors. It should retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets, because a malformed request fails identically on attempt five. Please also test the idempotency key header retry logic, since I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds server-side. Please ticket the metrics gap too.
